Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We attached our latest Order Form redline (FS-OrderForm-v3-redline.pdf) and a short note from Legal. Two open items we want to flag so your team can advise:

1) Governing law / venue — Finsight prefers Delaware law for commercial agreements and is asking for exclusive jurisdiction of Delaware courts for any court proceedings.
2) Dispute resolution — we propose AAA arbitration (commercial rules) with seat in New York for arbitrable claims. However, we also want a carveout so that either party can seek emergency injunctive relief in court (we suggested courts of the State of Delaware).

We understand Redwood typically prefers California law and county/state courts in the Bay Area for emergency relief carveouts. Can you confirm Redwood's position on: (a) whether Redwood will accept Delaware governing law, and (b) the specific wording you'd accept for an equitable relief carveout so both sides are protected?

Timing: procurement would like final language this week so we can get to countersignature. Appreciate a redline or note from your legal team.

Aaron —

Appreciate the redline and the heads up. Quick summary from our side and what Legal needs to consider:

- Governing law: Redwood typically prefers California law (CA substantive law is what our template uses). We are open to discussing Delaware, but need confirmation from legal on downstream impacts for indemnities and injunctive remedies.

- Arbitration / venue: Redwood is fine with arbitration for most contract disputes, but we require an explicit carveout that permits either party to seek injunctive or equitable relief in court to preserve IP and confidentiality remedies. Our usual drafting limits the carveout to \"injunctive and other equitable relief to protect proprietary rights, privacy/confidentiality obligations, and source code or model theft\" and reserves venue to a Northern California federal court (we typically name the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California).

- Practical ask: can we accept Delaware law if Finsight will: (a) accept Northern District of California as the exclusive forum for any court actions seeking equitable relief (injunctions), and (b) limit the carveout to those narrow categories (IP/confidentiality)? If not, please propose alternative wording that constrains forum-shopping while preserving emergency relief.

I'll loop Legal if you send suggested redline language for the carveout. If you want to trade venue instead (Delaware courts) we need Finsight Legal to accept Redwood's proposed narrow-purpose carveout language. Procurement timeline noted — we will try to move quickly.

Best,

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finsight.com>

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick responses and for proposing narrow language. Finsight Legal is prepared to accept Redwood's carveout relating to injunctive relief so long as we retain Delaware substantive law and the ability to seek emergency relief in a Delaware court. Proposed compromise:

- Governing law: Delaware.
- Arbitration: AAA (Commercial Rules), seat of arbitration New York, NY, for arbitrable disputes.
- Injunctive relief carveout: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Section shall prevent either party from seeking injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its intellectual property, trade secrets, or confidential information. For purposes of such court proceedings, the parties agree that the United States District Court for the District of Delaware or the Delaware Court of Chancery shall have exclusive jurisdiction."

We understand your preference for Northern District of California; however, given FinSight's corporate governance and outside counsel preferences, Delaware provides a predictable procedural path for injunctive remedies in our view. If Redwood can accept Delaware courts for injunctive relief only (with Delaware governing law overall), we will incorporate your narrow-purpose carveout language and circulate a final countersignature-ready Order Form.

Please confirm by EOD and, if accepted, we'll prepare a DocuSign envelope and share the link (we've included one in related_links).

Regards,
Laura Chen
